issues.legal_issue: A general proposal in a master plan to widen a road does not prohibit use of nearby land when the plan does not specifically indicate that the land is affected and no more detailed zonal plan has been prepared.
material_facts: The owners applied for sanction to carry out repairs, additions and alterations to their building.
The master plan recommended increasing the width of a nearby road, but did not indicate that any part of the owners’ land would be taken up by the road.
No zonal development plan had been prepared for the area.
issues.conclusion: The proposed use of the owners’ land did not violate the planning restriction because neither plan specified a different use for that land.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 7 and 8 of the Delhi Development Act, the master plan provides a broad framework, while a zonal development plan can identify the approximate location and extent of proposed land uses and land reserved for roads. Section 14 prohibits a use different from a particular use specified in an operative plan; a general proposal about a road’s width, without identifying the land affected, does not prohibit all use of adjoining land. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.building_plan_sanction_application: An owner applied for approval to carry out building work on land or a building.
predicates.master_plan_lacks_specific_land_designat: The master plan made a general proposal affecting the area but did not identify the particular land as being allocated or reserved for that proposal.
predicates.no_zonal_plan_prepared: No more detailed plan specifying land uses for the relevant zone had been prepared.

issues.definition: When an owner seeks approval for building work, a general master-plan proposal that does not identify the particular land does not prohibit its use if no more detailed zonal plan has been prepared.

issues.legal_issue: A building-plan sanction may not be refused on the ground that proposed work violates another law when the work does not contravene any applicable law or other statutory ground for refusal.
material_facts: The owners submitted plans for repairs, additions and alterations to their building.
The Commissioner refused sanction, relying on the proposed widening of a nearby road in the master plan.
The master plan did not indicate that the owners’ land was affected by the proposed road, and no zonal development plan had been prepared for the area.
The Commissioner had also notified the owners that the building required urgent repairs and that repairs should be carried out after obtaining sanction.
issues.conclusion: The refusal was not justified; the High Court was entitled to direct the Corporation to approve the plans and grant sanction, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 336(1) and 336(2)(a) of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, sanction must be granted unless the proposed building or work contravenes a specified statutory ground, including a bylaw or another law. Section 340 provides a further ground in the circumstances it describes. Because the proposed work did not violate section 14 of the Delhi Development Act, it did not contravene another law for purposes of section 336(2)(a). No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.building_plan_sanction_application: An owner applied to the relevant authority for sanction to carry out building work.
predicates.asserted_refusal_ground_is_plan_conflict: The authority relied on an alleged conflict between the proposed work and a planning document as its ground for refusing sanction.
predicates.proposed_work_does_not_violate_other_law: The proposed work did not contravene an applicable law or other statutory ground for refusing sanction.

issues.definition: When an owner applies for building-plan sanction and the authority relies on a planning conflict that does not amount to a violation of another applicable law, sanction must be granted.
